newsitem.title: FRANCE: Debate on EU council and ECB already done - Santer.
newsitem.headline: Debate on EU council and ECB already done - Santer.

text.p: Creation of an EU council to coordinate economic policy in the euro single currency zone was agreed to at the same time as the EU's Maastricht Treaty, European Commission President Jacques Santer said on Monday.

The debate took place back then, and the treaty allows for the council structure, alongside the European central bank, to have powers in multilateral surveillance, economic convergence and broad economic goals, Santer told French daily Liberation.
"This discussion on an 'economic government' took place when the Maastricht Treaty was being negotiated and the idea of an 'economic government' was ruled out," he said in an interview.

"Let's stick to what the treaty says. Yes, the ECB (future European central bank) will be indepdedent, but the council of ministers will be strengthened. It (the council) will have powers in the area of multilateral surveilliance, convergence programmes and major economic objectives," Santer was quoted as saying.
"Mechanisms, therefore, exist for a dialogue between the council of ministers and the ECB," he said.
France says the council, gathering ministers at an informal level, is absolutely necessary and has backing among EU partners in this.

This issue, which has provoked constant reminders from the German Bundesbank that the independent ECB must be protected from political bodies, could be raised at a Brussels meeting of European Union finance ministers on Monday, but is not slated for formal discussion.
Santer said the issue of the council was dealt with and would only be put into action once the single currency came into existence, which is scheduled for January 1999.
"At this moment, certain forms of cooperation between member countries will be able to fully develop," Santer said.

Asked if there was a risk of an "arrogant" European central bank answerable to no one, Santer said "no, because there are mechanisms ready and waiting. The president of the ECB will be able to come to the council of ministers, and a dialogue can be opened between the bodies."
Santer also said the German people's hesitancy about the advent of the euro still had yet to be dealt with.

"An information campaign is needed so that the Germans can understand that the euro is in their interest. This job has not yet been done. Chancellor (Helmut) Kohl has to get involved and convince them," he added.

Asked if the relative strength or weakness of the future euro currency was purely a French debate, Santer replied "Yes. What counts is achieving economic and monetary union and not overloading the issue with other considerations which add to the confusion".
On British participation, he said "If it's in the interests of the City of London or industry to participate, the British government will join the euro.
